Operators, creative mode, elytras, vehicles and portals are left out. Never acted on automatically: an ender pearl stasis chamber can look like a teleport.

Mining counts are the game's own and arrive when the server saves, a few minutes behind.

joinPassword.restartToAskPlayersFor: Restart to ask players for a password?
joinPassword.playersSetAPasswordThe: Players set a password the first time they join and give it every time after. Worth having when Mojang authentication is off, because without it the server has only a name to go on and anyone who knows a listed name can use it.
joinPassword.bedrockHasNoEquivalentIt: Bedrock has no equivalent. It loads neither plugins nor mods, so the player list and the addresses it is bound to are what closes this server.
joinPassword.thisServerRunsNeitherPlugins: This server runs neither plugins nor mods, so there is nothing to install. Switch it to Paper, or to a mod loader, from Settings first.
joinPassword.theirPasswordCanAppearIn: Their password can appear in the server log, which the Console screen shows - it is hidden only by a library Modrinth does not carry, so treat these as passwords for this server and nothing else.
joinPassword.playersWillDrop: {count, plural, one {# player is} other {# players are}} connected and will be disconnected.
joinPassword.restartsToApply: The server restarts to apply it.
joinPassword.noAnswer: Polaris did not answer. Reload the page and try again.
joinPassword.modOn: Everybody registers with /register the next time they join. While the server cannot reach Polaris, nobody can join and it does not start.
joinPassword.modOnListed: Everybody registers with /register the next time they join, and the passwords kept by {name} stop working. While the server cannot reach Polaris, nobody can join and it does not start.
joinPassword.modOff: Anybody on the player list gets in on their name alone afterwards. The passwords stay here in case you turn it back on.
joinPassword.noBuild: {name} has no build for the release this server runs. The server would start without it and nobody would be asked for a password, so this is left off rather than left looking on.
joinPassword.noBuildFor: {name} has no build for the release this server runs ({version}). The server would start without it and nobody would be asked for a password, so this is left off rather than left looking on.
joinPassword.guardOn: Everybody sets their own the next time they join.
joinPassword.guardOff: Anybody on the player list gets in on their name alone afterwards.
joinPassword.foreign: Players already log in with <mono>{name}</mono>, which Polaris does not manage. Remove it from the Mods screen to use a login from here instead.
joinPassword.usesLogin: Uses Polaris login: players get <mono>/register</mono> and <mono>/login</mono> with text passwords, kept in Polaris so you can reset one here. While the server cannot reach Polaris, nobody can join and the server does not start.
joinPassword.still: Players still log in with <mono>{name}</mono>. Turning this on replaces it, and every player registers again.
joinPassword.stillNumeric: Players still log in with <mono>{name}</mono> and numeric passwords. Turning this on replaces it, and every player registers again.
joinPassword.installs: Installs <mono>{name}</mono> from Modrinth, which the Mods screen shows afterwards like anything else on the list. A release it has no build for is skipped and the server starts without it rather than failing to start, so check the Mods screen once the server is back up.
joinPassword.triggerHelp: Players register with <mono>/trigger register set 1234</mono> and come back with <mono>/trigger login set 1234</mono>. The password can only be a number: this runs as a data pack, and the only thing vanilla lets an unauthenticated player send the server is a scoreboard value. Writing <mono>/trigger register</mono> without <mono>set</mono> does not fail - it registers the password 1, and the next login says the password is wrong.
joinPassword.pluginHelp: Players register on their first join with the commands <mono>{name}</mono> documents on its Modrinth page. Tell them before turning this on: nobody can look that up from inside the server they have just been locked out of.

The link needs no account here.

reset.itWasNotBuiltFrom: It was not built from a blueprint, or was created before Polaris recorded which one.
reset.theMapItIsOn: The map it is on is kept, so you can switch back to it under World.
reset.playerSlotsAndEverythingElse: Player slots and everything else on Settings are left as they are.
reset.saveThisServerAsA: Save this server as a template
reset.keepsWhatYouChangedFrom: Keeps what you changed from the blueprint's defaults - not this server's address, players or ports.
reset.inventoriesEnderChestsStatsAnd: Inventories, ender chests, stats and advancements come across. The server has to be running for the copy to be made.
reset.aBuiltMapComesWith: A built map comes with its own spawn and its own idea of what you start with, so everyone begins it fresh.
reset.bedrockKeepsPlayerDataInside: Bedrock keeps player data inside the world itself, so a new map always starts everyone over.
reset.builtFromOn: It is built from {name} on {map} now.
reset.memoryGiven: The rebuilt server is given <memory></memory> of memory.

reset.restartWarningPlaying: The server restarts onto a new map, so anybody playing is disconnected - {count} {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} on it right now. The map it is on now is kept and you can switch back to it under World.

optimize.aWorldKeepsEveryChunk: A world keeps every chunk anybody has ever loaded, and most of what gets loaded is scenery nobody walks into. Those chunks generate again, identically, the moment somebody goes there - so removing them costs nothing and usually takes a world down by half or more. Anything a player has stood in is kept, along with spawn, forced chunks and everywhere people log out.
optimize.theServerStopsWhileThis: The server stops while this runs and starts again afterwards.
optimize.keepItTidyOnIts: Keep it tidy on its own
optimize.runsWhileTheServerIs: Runs while the server is already stopped and never stops one to do it, so a server that is always up is never touched by this.
optimize.optimizeThisWorldOnIts: Optimize this world on its own
optimize.theLastRunDidNot: The last run did not work
optimize.lastRunNothing: Last run {date}: nothing to take out.

domain.noNameYetGiveIt: No name yet. Give it one and Polaris writes the records.
domain.sharesPort25565WithThe: Shares port 25565 with the other Java servers, so the address needs no port and no DNS record of its own. Players connect from the router's address, so the player list cannot be bound to addresses.
domain.giveItItsOwnPort: Give it its own port, or put it behind the shared one: an address with no port, and no DNS record per server. Its player list can then only be closed by username.
domain.willConnect: Players will connect to <address></address>. The old name keeps resolving until you remove its record.

login.readFailed: Could not read the login state

engine.theServerRestartsToLoad: The server restarts to load the change, and everybody on it is disconnected for a moment.
engine.onThisNeoforgeServerPolaris: On this NeoForge server, Polaris's own mod sends buried ore as plain rock, so X-Ray shows nothing but Polaris's honeypots, and reports whoever digs at ore they could not see. On by default; it takes effect on the next start. Movement and combat checks need Paper or another plugin server.
engine.itRunsOnPaperPurpur: It runs on Paper, Purpur, Pufferfish, Leaf, Folia and Spigot, and its anti-xray on NeoForge 1.21.4. Switch the server to one of them in Settings to use it.
engine.itNeedsThisPolarisTo: It needs this Polaris to have a public address: the server downloads the plugin from it when it starts. Set one under Domains.
engine.turnedOn: On. The server is restarting with it.
engine.turnedOff: Off. The server is restarting without it.
engine.about: Checks every player's movement and combat against what the game allows, packet by packet: flying, speed, reach, killaura, no-fall and the rest. Runs on the server, compensating for each player's latency, so a laggy player is not taken for a cheater. It also sends buried ore as plain rock, so X-Ray shows nothing but Polaris's honeypots. On by default; a server made before it gets it on its next start. While it is on, the server downloads it from this Polaris each time it starts, and does not start if Polaris cannot be reached.

spigot.mostPluginsArePublishedHere: Most plugins are published here rather than on Modrinth. They are installed on the next restart, by number, and SpigotMC says which releases each one was tested on - which is its author saying so, not a build this can check.
spigot.nothingCameBackSpigotmcMay: Nothing came back. SpigotMC may be unreachable from here rather than empty.
spigot.installedWhenTheServerNext: Installed when the server next restarts.

events.anAutomaticEventOnlyStarts: An automatic event only starts while enough players are actually playing - somebody who has not moved or turned for a while does not count.
events.inTheHoursBelowAn: In the hours below, an event is drawn from the ones ticked every so often, weighted, and never the same kind twice in a row.
events.skippedAndWrittenInThe: Skipped, and written in the history, when too few are playing at that time.
events.givenTheNextTimeEach: Given the next time each player is on. Kept for 14 days.
events.noEventsHaveRunOn: No events have run on this server yet.

mining-rush.label: Mining rush
mining-rush.summary: Most ore mined in the time wins. Any ore scores by its rarity, or pick diamonds or ancient debris only. Players caught by Anti X-Ray or the anti-cheat during it are left off the podium.

mob-hunt.label: Mob hunt
mob-hunt.summary: Most hostile mobs killed wins, the rare and dangerous ones worth more, or a single kind of mob.

supply-drop.label: Supply drop
supply-drop.summary: A chest of loot lands somewhere in the Overworld. Where is revealed in three steps, a beam of light marks it, and the first player to open it keeps what is inside.

blood-moon.label: Blood moon
blood-moon.summary: Night falls with rain and waves of mobs rise around every player on the surface. Survive to dawn without dying; the podium goes to the most kills.

world-boss.label: World boss
world-boss.summary: A boss with a health bar everybody sees appears near the players. Damage dealt close to it is counted; if it falls, the podium goes by damage and everybody who hit it is rewarded.

fishing.label: Fishing contest
fishing.summary: Most catches with a fishing rod wins.

trivia.label: Trivia
trivia.summary: Questions about Minecraft, or a scrambled word, in the chat. The first right answer takes the round. Add questions of your own.

explorer.label: Explorer
explorer.summary: Travel the farthest on foot, swimming, riding or gliding - or race to a set of coordinates announced at the start.

happy-hour.label: Happy hour
happy-hour.summary: Haste, luck and other effects for everybody for a while. No winner - a good filler between competitions.

king-of-the-hill.label: King of the hill
king-of-the-hill.summary: A marked circle appears. The longest time spent inside it wins - so it is worth defending.

treasure-hunt.label: Treasure hunt
treasure-hunt.summary: Loot chests are hidden on open ground around the players, told in clues that get sharper as it goes. Whoever opens the most wins, and keeps what is inside.

gathering.label: Gathering
gathering.summary: One material is announced - wheat, logs, cobblestone, iron... Whoever gathers the most of it wins. Nothing is taken from anybody.

rare-catch.label: Rare catch
rare-catch.summary: A fishing race for one treasure - a name tag, a saddle, an enchanted book... The first to fish it up wins, and keeps it.

xp-boost.label: Experience boost
xp-boost.summary: Extra experience for every mob killed and every ore mined, for everybody, for a while. No winner - a good filler between competitions.

waves.label: Horde defence
waves.summary: A defence point is marked away from every home and waves of monsters come for it, each bigger and stronger than the last. Everybody who holds the point is rewarded; the podium goes to the most kills.

meteor-shower.label: Meteor shower
meteor-shower.summary: Meteors of ore fall one after another on open ground away from every home, each marked by a beam of light. Whoever mines the most meteor blocks wins.

parkour.label: Parkour race
parkour.summary: A jump course is built high in the air. Players type join in the chat to take part and are taken to the start; the fastest to the finish wins, and a fall only sends you back to your last checkpoint.

spleef.label: Spleef
spleef.summary: The floor is lava: a snow floor is built high in the air and players who type join get a shovel that only breaks that snow. Dig it out from under the others - whoever falls through is out and sent back - and the last one standing wins.

team-duel.label: Team duel
team-duel.summary: Players who type join are split into two teams in an arena built in the sky, each given the same sword and shield. The team with more eliminations wins; the podium goes by each player's own. Nobody loses anything: a player low on health is sent back to their side, and inventories are kept whatever happens.

build-battle.label: Build battle
build-battle.summary: Players who type join each get a plot in the sky, a theme and a kit of coloured glass. When the time is up everybody tours the plots and votes for the best in the chat. Only the kit can be built with; nothing of anybody's is used or taken.

facts.regeneration: Regeneration (health comes back on its own)
facts.happyHour: Everybody on gets {effects} until it ends, including whoever joins meanwhile.
facts.chestsHidden: {count} {count, plural, one {chest} other {chests}} hidden up to {distance} blocks from the players, on open natural ground well away from anybody's bed.
facts.clues: Clues come in three steps: how far and which way, then the area, then the exact spot; a beam of light marks the ones left in the last minutes. A player close to one sees the way in their action bar.
facts.chestsCleared: A chest is only put where there is air, and one nobody opened is taken away at the end. An opened chest stays: what is inside is the finder's.
facts.materialRandom: The material is drawn from the list each time and announced when the countdown starts.
facts.gatheringScore: Scored by what each player holds at the end minus what they held when it began, and never more than they picked up during it - a stack taken out of a chest does not count. Nothing is taken from anybody.
facts.rareCatch: The first player to fish up {treasure} wins, and keeps it. Taking one out of a chest, or dropping one and picking it up, does not count.
facts.xpBoost: Everybody on gets {extra} until it ends. Nothing is ever taken away; an ore block placed during it is not paid for again.
facts.waves: {waves} waves, {minutes} minutes at most. A wave ends when all of it is killed, or after two minutes.
facts.wavesPoint: The point is on open, flat ground the world made, at least 96 blocks from any online player's bed. Only monsters that cannot break blocks come - no creepers, endermen or ravagers - and every one of them is removed when it ends.
facts.keepInventory: Keep inventory is on while it runs, so dying costs nothing; the server's own setting comes back afterwards. Java 1.17 or later.
facts.meteors: {meteors} meteors of {size} ore blocks each, landing over the first three quarters of it. Each block mined near a meteor scores 1; ore placed near one is taken off.
facts.meteorsLand: Meteors land on open, flat ground the world made, at least 48 blocks from any online player's bed, and ore is only ever put where there was air. What nobody mined is taken away at the end - only blocks still exactly the meteor's ore - and nothing else is touched.
facts.pickaxes: Diamond and emerald ore need an iron pickaxe, ancient debris a diamond one.
facts.parkour: {jumps} jumps, {difficulty}, built about {height} blocks up. A fall lands on a net and goes back to the last checkpoint.
facts.spleef: A {size} by {size} snow floor about {height} blocks up. Falling through it is being out; the last one on it wins.
facts.joinCountdown: Only players who type join (or unirse) in the chat during the countdown - at least {seconds} seconds - take part. They are taken there and brought back to exactly where they were when it ends, even after a restart.
facts.stageBuilt: It is built only in empty air, over open ground away from everybody's bed, and taken down block by block afterwards - only what it placed. Inside, nobody can take damage and everybody is in adventure mode; their game mode is given back after.
facts.spleefShovel: Players get a marked shovel that only breaks the snow; it is cleared at the end, and nothing else of theirs is touched. Needs Java 1.14.4 or newer; before 1.20.5 the snow drops snowballs when dug.
facts.parkourItems: Nobody's items are touched. Needs Java 1.14.4 or newer.
facts.duelJoin: Only players who type join (or unirse) in the chat during the countdown take part. They are split into two teams and taken to an arena built 30 blocks up, over open ground away from anybody's bed.
facts.duelKit: Everybody gets the same {kit} sword and a shield. A player down to {hearts} {hearts, plural, one {heart} other {hearts}} is out: the other team scores, the rival who brought them down gets the elimination, and they are sent back to their side, healed. The team with more wins; the podium goes by eliminations.
facts.duelKeepInventory: Keep inventory is on while it lasts and put back after, so even a death in the arena keeps everything.
facts.duelNeeds: Needs Player versus player allowed in Settings, and Minecraft 1.16 or later. Up to 16 players.
facts.buildJoin: Only players who type join (or unirse) in the chat during the countdown take part. Each gets a plot on a platform built 30 blocks up, over open ground away from anybody's bed.
facts.buildPlanMine: A theme from your list, a {size} by {size} plot, 16 kinds of glass and a brush; {minutes} minutes to build, then {seconds} seconds touring the plots and voting in the chat - one vote each, not for your own plot. Most votes wins.
facts.buildPlanBuiltIn: A built-in theme, a {size} by {size} plot, 16 kinds of glass and a brush; {minutes} minutes to build, then {seconds} seconds touring the plots and voting in the chat - one vote each, not for your own plot. Most votes wins.
facts.buildGlass: Only the kit's glass can be placed: builders play in adventure mode, where their own blocks cannot be put down at all, so nothing of theirs is used or left on a plot. Glass broken by hand drops nothing, so no kit leaves a plot either.
facts.buildNeeds: Needs Minecraft 1.16 or later. Up to 12 builders.
facts.arena: Nothing of anybody's is touched. The arena goes only where the air was empty, and comes down block kind by block kind; only the event's own marked kit is taken back; each player is sent back to exactly where they stood, in their own game mode, with whatever they dropped. Somebody offline at the end finds it still standing when they log in, and is sent back then.
facts.overworld: Happens in the Overworld; only players there take part.
facts.rankedFrom: Ranked from {score} {unit}; below that, no podium and no prize.
facts.startsWith: Starts on its own only with {count} {count, plural, one {player} other {players}} actually playing, and not while somebody is in a fight.
facts.hostileMobs: Needs the server above Peaceful, where hostile mobs exist.
facts.unrankedAfk: Nobody playing in creative or spectator, caught by the anti-cheat, or AFK the whole time is ranked.
facts.unranked: Nobody playing in creative or spectator, or caught by the anti-cheat, is ranked.

editor.everybodyWhoSurvivedTheNight: Everybody who survived the night with a kill.
editor.everybodyWhoHeldThePoint: Everybody who held the point through a wave and fought.
editor.everybodyWhoJoinedAndCleared: Everybody who joined and cleared at least one jump.

hunt.hostile: Every hostile mob, the dangerous worth more

waveMix.undead: The undead: zombies, husks, skeletons, strays

meteorOre.common: Common: coal, iron, copper (1.17+), gold, redstone, lapis

place.drop: It lands up to the distance below around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.boss: It appears about 20 blocks around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.finish: The finish is set the distance below around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.circle: The circle is drawn about 30 blocks around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.point: The point is marked about 50 blocks around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.meteor: Each meteor lands up to the distance below around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.openGround: It is built over open ground around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.arena: The arena is built 30 blocks up, about 30 blocks around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.
place.plots: The plots are built 30 blocks up, about 30 blocks around a player who is in the Overworld when it starts.

editor.kitHint: The same for everybody, and taken back at the end.
editor.outAtHint: 1 to 6. A player this low is sent back to their side, healed, and the other team scores.
editor.plotSizeHint: 7 to 15 a side, as tall as it is wide
editor.themesHint: One a line; one is drawn each time.
editor.builtInThemes: One of 30 built-in themes, in the players' language.
editor.materialHint: Announced when the countdown starts. Only what is gathered during the event counts.
editor.catchHint: One treasure comes up about once in 120 catches, any of them about once in 25 - in open water, more often with Luck of the Sea. Give it 20 minutes or more.
editor.perKillHint: Experience points, 0 to 100. A zombie gives 5.
editor.perOreHint: Experience points, 0 to 100. Coal ore gives up to 2.
